builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AgentPProf: Semantic Profiler for Long Horizon AI Agents
summary: Replaces per-execution debugging and tracing with cross-run profiling that aggregates agent trajectories into pprof-compatible flame graphs via recursive operation segmentation at task boundaries. Costs an additional segmentation and aggregation pipeline over collected trajectories, with profiling overhead the authors describe as practical but which still requires instrumented, consistently logged agent runs. Segmentation can misattribute work when task boundaries are ambiguous (0.764 F1 against human annotations indicates residual segmentation error), which can misdirect optimization effort toward wrong hotspots.
rationale: The tool is open source and addresses a real production need (cost and failure attribution across runs), but its value depends on the reader having enough long-horizon agent traffic and on segmentation accuracy for their workload, so it warrants a small-scale pilot before adoption.

claims.statement: Replaces per-execution debugging and tracing with cross-run profiling that aggregates agent trajectories into pprof-compatible flame graphs via recursive operation segmentation at task boundaries. Costs an additional segmentation and aggregation pipeline over collected trajectories, with profiling overhead the authors describe as practical but which still requires instrumented, consistently logged agent runs. Segmentation can misattribute work when task boundaries are ambiguous (0.764 F1 against human annotations indicates residual segmentation error), which can misdirect optimization effort toward wrong hotspots.
Raises MAP by up to 56% on three problem-localization benchmarks; reaches 0.764 B3 F1 against human annotations on CodeTraceBench.
